request.state: The checked Can compiler revision is 309644a6881909d8dba32560bc6711f67e00a7ab. All 39 implementation source files total 71473 lines; its only locked package is itself. Dependency freedom is documented as current implementation, and no inspected user instruction mandates it. Can-specific duties are indentation/description grammar, recovery and lossless syntax, resolution/types/authority/effects and JS lowering. The audit separately identifies standard-format/algorithm implementations: SHA256, JSON read/write and repeated escaped-string decoding, LSP stdio/wire objects, command options/help/shell scripts, source-map VLQ, file URIs, temporary replacement and literal format validation. Executed small public probes show: the legal source escapes \b\f and paired \uD83D\uDE00 become bf and two U+FFFD characters in emitted JS; a three-emoji URL field default causes a byte-boundary panic; bracketed non-IP authority and out-of-range numeric port pass; LSP responds after replacing malformed UTF-8; formatting replaces a 0600 file with mode0644. The 89 unit tests were green. These reproduced gaps coexist with substantial useful tests. Official crate documentation/source confirms that sha2 hashes SHA256, serde_json handles typed JSON and raw_value/string decoding, url provides WHATWG parsing/file conversion, tempfile offers persistence in one directory, and lsp-types defines protocol structures. No alternative was installed or timed. Current custom JSON retains member order and duplicate members, and every numeric lexeme; depth64 and LSP body64MiB are existing bounds. A plain serde_json Value conversion is not full parity. The inspected lsp-server0.10 represents IDs by i32/string and doesn't enforce that body size cap in its framing implementation. Each option must retain ordered diagnostics, Can codes, exact required IDs, resource bounds, initialization/shutdown, exit statuses0/10/2 and emitted semantics. The scope is recommending investigation follow-through; production sources are unchanged.

approach.instructions: Given those observations, costs and fixed behaviors, select the most defensible proposal for what compiler maintenance should do next.

criteria.CUSTOM: Continue the dependency-free approach, correcting defects and strengthening external-standard fixtures. It minimizes external version/build risk and existing-interface disruption, at the price of ongoing ownership of generic protocols and algorithms.
criteria.FRAMEWORK: Coordinate migration to established syntax/incremental, JavaScript AST and server frameworks. Shared framework facilities may help future tooling, but the larger change must reproduce grammar recovery and generated behavior and currently has no measured necessity.
criteria.TARGETED: Replace selected commodity implementations with focused crates through staged compatibility adapters and independent gates. This reduces repeated standard implementations but adds dependency upkeep, build/size uncertainty and explicit contract-preservation work.
